name: Carpentersville
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Carpentersville, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Carpentersville, IL: Winterville in Triangle Park, the Riverside Parade of Lights, Santa at the Rakow Center and trolleys nearby.
lede: Carpentersville starts its Christmas season in Triangle Park on Main Street, where the village lights its tree and Santa waits in his house before the Riverside Parade of Lights crosses the Fox River.
celebrates: The Village of Carpentersville hosts Winterville in the Park each December at Triangle Park, where West Main Street meets South Washington Street. The evening brings the village tree lighting with the Village Board, visits with Santa, carolers, hot cocoa, holiday treats and local food vendors. Winterville ends just as the Riverside Parade of Lights arrives, a parade that starts in West Dundee, crosses the Main Street bridge in Carpentersville and finishes in East Dundee. The Dundee Township Park District adds more at the Rakow Center on Barrington Avenue, where Theater on the Fox stages a holiday musical and families can register for Santa visits, stories and crafts.
lastyear: In 2025, Winterville in the Park opened with the tree lighting at Triangle Park, according to a recap posted on Explore Elgin Area. Kids visited Santa in his house, wrote letters and mailed them in a North Pole mailbox with a Carpentersville Express stamp. Café Té Latte poured cocoa and cider, Dirty Dough brought cookies, the Lakewood Elementary School Choir sang, and The Home Depot ran a kids' craft station. The Daily Herald listed the Riverside Parade of Lights for 6:30 pm on Saturday, December 6, 2025.
facts: Carpentersville began in 1837, when Charles and Daniel Carpenter camped on the east bank of the Fox River to wait out spring floods and decided to stay. The settlement was first called Carpenters' Grove. Charles's son, Julius Angelo Carpenter, built its first store, bridge and factory, and he paid for a wooden bridge over the river where the Main Street bridge stands today. Until the 1950s, Main Street had the only highway bridge across the Fox between Algonquin and Dundee, the same bridge the Riverside Parade of Lights now crosses.
trains: Carpentersville once had its own electric railway. In 1896 an interurban line opened from Elgin, running four miles to the Illinois Iron and Bolt foundry on Main Street, and families rode its summer cars to Elgin's Trout Park. A 1933 tornado wrecked a bridge on the line. Today the Fox River Trolley Museum in South Elgin runs antique cars on track the Aurora, Elgin and Fox River Electric built in 1896, and it runs Santa's Trolley Express at Christmas. Carpentersville has no Metra station, but Metra runs decorated Holiday Trains each December.

kidfact: Carpentersville started because of a flood. In 1837 the Carpenter brothers could not get their oxcart across the flooded Fox River, so they camped on the riverbank and ended up staying.
faq: Winterville in the Park is the Village of Carpentersville's holiday kickoff at Triangle Park. It brings the village tree lighting with the Village Board, visits with Santa, carolers, hot cocoa, seasonal treats and local food vendors. It is timed to end just before the Riverside Parade of Lights crosses the Main Street bridge. Check the village Winterville page for this year's schedule.
Where is Triangle Park in Carpentersville?

Triangle Park sits at the intersection of West Main Street and South Washington Street in Carpentersville, near the Main Street bridge over the Fox River. Explore Elgin Area lists its address as 39 E. Main Street. It is the home of Winterville in the Park and the village Christmas tree.
Where can I watch the Riverside Parade of Lights in Carpentersville?

The Riverside Parade of Lights starts on South Lincoln Avenue in West Dundee, heads north to the Main Street bridge in Carpentersville, then turns south on Washington and Water Streets into East Dundee. In Carpentersville, families watch near the Main Street bridge and Triangle Park. The Northern Kane County Chamber posts approximate times each year based on past parades.

The Rakow Center is the Dundee Township Park District's main building, at 665 Barrington Avenue in Carpentersville, at the corner of Routes 25 and 68. It holds an indoor pool and the Adult Activities Center, where Theater on the Fox performs and the park district hosts holiday programs such as the Jolly Stop with Santa.
Can kids send a letter to Santa in Carpentersville?

Yes. At Winterville in 2025, kids wrote letters to Santa and dropped them in his North Pole mailbox, which came with a Carpentersville Express stamp for special delivery. The Dundee Township Park District's Jolly Stop at the Rakow Center also has Santa's Mailbox along with a holiday craft and Christmas carols.
